title: Micro starter templates and focused examples for SDK streaming, retries, and CLI ergonomics
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Create a set of compact, copy-paste-ready starter templates and cookbook snippets that demo best practices for the Redwood SDKs across Next.js (TypeScript), FastAPI (Python), Go HTTP servers, and a CLI reference. Focus areas: streaming ergonomics (client + server patterns), recommended retry/backoff configurations for transient errors, cancellation and context propagation, and minimal examples showing how to integrate SDK features like streaming token callbacks, function/tool calling stubs, and embedding usage. The goal is to reduce time-to-first-success for new users and surface production patterns we recommend in docs and quickstarts.
acceptance_criteria: Four distinct templates exist: Next.js (TSX), FastAPI (Python async), Go HTTP server, and a small CLI (Python or Go). Each is under 200 lines with clear TODOs for customization.
Each template contains a short README with: copy-paste install, env setup, how to run locally, and a one-minute demo script.
Retry policy examples are provided (exponential backoff + jitter) and wired into each template with toggles; documented expected trade-offs and recommended default values.
Streaming example demonstrates both chunked UI streaming (Next.js) and server-side async iteration (FastAPI/Go) with graceful cancellation and KV-cache header hints.
CLI example shows token usage, local caching for embeddings, and a recommended backoff wrapper for CLI network calls.
All code snippets have linters passing and basic unit/integration smoke tests included (scripts that run locally).
Design/Docs sign-off: docs@redwood has reviewed READMEs and approved copy and UX flow.
Publish artifacts to github.com/redwood/integrations/examples with clear licensing and issue template for contributions.
implementation_notes: Keep templates intentionally minimal: focus on patterns rather than full-featured apps. Use SDK stable APIs and avoid experimental flags. Where behavior differs across languages, add a short 'gotchas' note. Prefer async/await patterns for Python/TS and context.Context for Go. Add a single helper for retries that can be imported into examples. Reference runtime batching/kv-cache docs for header suggestions.
